title: Exact null spellings
lead: `nullTokens` keys are the vocabulary entries (`null`, `NA`, empty, ...), matched case-insensitively after trimming, so `NULL`, `Null`, `null` and ` NULL ` all count under one key, and the counts include all-null (separator) rows. A consumer that treats only one spelling as null cannot get its count. Add the exact spellings as seen, and counts that leave out all-null rows. **Not in this slice:** changing the vocabulary or how values are classified.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A library consumer treats only the exact token `NULL` as null and keeps other spellings as text. It can only report squalify's counts as upper bounds today, and has to subtract the separator rows itself.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: - `FieldAccumulator`, `DelimitedPass` (the layout counts), `ValueClassifier` (return the matched raw text), the descriptor and descriptor.md, README

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- A column with `NULL`, `Null`, `null` and ` NULL ` reports each exact spelling with its own count, next to today's key `null`, which is unchanged.
- In a file with all-null separator rows, each field's null counts are also reported without those rows, and the two add up.
- Values that differ only in surrounding whitespace are reported as distinct spellings (or the trim rule is stated; pick one and document it).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
- Keep today's `nullTokens` as is, so existing descriptors and goldens keep their meaning; add the new map beside it.
- Decide with the owner whether this rides with sq-32 (compact field profiles), which changes the same field block.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Build, test and format pass; `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: The owner commits. Do not commit; never add Co-Authored-By or similar lines.
